On 2022-05-05, the user asked to add material about Electronic Performance Support Systems (EPSS) to an existing literature review. The material describes EPSS as computer-based, on-the-job, just-in-time support that provides resources such as instructional materials, reference guides, and job aids across desktop computers, laptops, tablets, and smartphones. It argues EPSS may improve performance, productivity, and work quality, while noting that implementation depends on user acceptance and use.

The EPSS literature-review draft identifies perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use as key technology-acceptance factors, citing Davis (1989), Davis et al. (1989), and Mathieson (1991). It also cites studies on additional adoption factors: interfunctional communication for CRM (Ashraf et al., 2017); performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and social influence for mobile learning (Chao, 2019); cost and employee satisfaction for ERP (Kwak et al., 2011); and cost, technology acceptance, and employee satisfaction for eCRM (Navimipour and Soltani, 2016).

The EPSS literature-review draft notes organizational and contextual influences on technology adoption, citing organizational learning capacity (Robey et al., 2000), attitudes toward complex technological innovations (Teo et al., 2006), and training, top-management support, and compatibility with business processes in ERP use (Rajan and Baral, 2015).

The EPSS literature-review draft states that instructional designers play a critical role in EPSS design and implementation. It cites Boling et al. (2017) on designer judgments about learners, learning environments, and learning objectives; Gal and Nachmias (2012) on user attitudes toward EPSS; Gal et al. (2017) on a tablet-based EPSS for technician training in the Israeli Air Force; and Klein and Kelly (2018) on instructional-design competencies.
